briefings.title: Arsenal of Freedom: Saronic Technologies
briefings.tldr: Secretary of War Pete Hegseth visited Saronic Technologies in Austin, Texas, on September 18, 2026, to praise the defense tech company's rapid scaling of autonomous maritime vessels and to highlight the Department of War's broader push to break through Pentagon bureaucracy by prioritizing commercial speed, non-traditional innovators, and domestic manufacturing.
briefings.summary_markdown:
## TL;DR
Secretary of War Pete Hegseth visited Saronic Technologies in Austin, Texas, on September 18, 2026, to praise the defense tech company's rapid scaling of autonomous maritime vessels and to highlight the Department of War's broader push to break through Pentagon bureaucracy by prioritizing commercial speed, non-traditional innovators, and domestic manufacturing.

## Saronic Technologies: Scale, Facilities, and Economic Impact
* **Austin Headquarters & Manufacturing:** 
  * Scaled to **1,200 Texas employees** operating **540,000 square feet** across Austin, with maritime trials conducted in Galveston.
  * Projected to generate over **$260 billion** in economic impact for Texas.
* **Port of Brownsville (Port Alpha):** 
  * Represents a **$3 billion investment**.
  * Creates up to **10,000 high-paying jobs** and **$160 billion in regional impact** for Cameron County.
  * Delivers **150,000 gross tons of new shipbuilding capacity**, which will double domestic shipbuilding.
* **Louisiana Expansion:** 
  * Involves a **$300+ million investment** to modernize the historic Gulf Craft Shipyard in Franklin and establish a new engineering hub in New Orleans.
  * Creates over **1,500 high-paying maritime careers** combining historic craft with robotics.
* **Supply Chain Footprint:** 
  * The Corsair USV is manufactured entirely with American materials and hands sourced through a network of **94 American suppliers across 27 American states**.

## Combat Deployments & Technological Milestones
* **First Combat Search and Rescue (CSAR):** 
  * In June, two U.S. Army AG-64 Apache pilots went down in contested waters near Oman. 
  * Saronic's **24-foot autonomous Corsair USV** (built in Austin) navigated forward and safely rescued the two pilots, marking the first known combat search and rescue mission executed by an autonomous vessel in American history.
* **First Sea Drone Combat Strike:** 
  * In July, CENTCOM employed the Corsair to strike a submarine and ship maintenance facility at the Bandar-e Abbas naval base in the Persian Gulf, marking the first operational employment of sea drones in U.S. military combat operations and degrading Iran's naval capabilities.
* **Vessel Portfolio & Production Speed:** 
  * Delivered over **300 combat-proven Corsairs**.
  * Rapidly fielded the **52-foot Mirage** and scaled blue-water reach with the **180-foot Marauder**, all built in under a year.

## Department of War Strategy & Acquisition Reform
* **War on Pentagon Bureaucracy:** 
  * Secretary Pete Hegseth and Chief Technology Officer Emil Michael are working to dismantle the legacy defense oligarchy, open up building access to fast runners, and move from bureaucracy to business.
* **Three Department Pillars:** 
  * Reviving the warrior ethos (focusing strictly on lethality over social engineering/DEI).
  * Rebuilding the military via generational funding investments.
  * Re-establishing deterrence through decisive hard power and sinking narco-terrorist boats rather than catch-and-release.
* **Procurement Shifts:** 
  * Providing larger, longer, and more predictable contracts to companies that deliver at pace and scale while investing in workers instead of stock buybacks.

## Workforce & Talent Pipeline
* **Veteran Leadership & Integration:** 
  * Founded and operated by Navy SEAL veteran and CEO Dino Mavrakis (eight combat tours) and Marine veteran Rob Layman.
  * Leverages the Department's SkillBridge program and Service Academies to create a premier talent pipeline.
* **Industrial Workforce Transition:** 
  * Actively transitioning skilled civilian American welders and machinists from the automotive and aerospace industries into cutting-edge naval shipbuilding.

## Notable Quotes

> "The last 15 minutes hasn't even been my words. This was a speech by Donald Rumsfeld, September 10th, 2001."
> — **Dino Mavrakis** (sharing an anecdote about acquisition reform)

> "Every helmet out there slinging lead on our behalf is doing it because of a hard hat enabling them that stands behind them. That's you, that's your mission inside this company with what you're building with these beautiful boats, ships, whatever the Navy calls them. Vessels, thank you very much. On behalf of our war fighters."
> — **Pete Hegseth**

> "We are a different department than we were two years ago. Night and day. You see, I don't, I don't care what name is on the side of a vessel or a missile or a ship. I just want the best."
> — **Pete Hegseth**

briefings.title: Bill Gurley: Searching for Feynman
briefings.tldr: Bill Gurley examines historical catastrophes (like the 737 MAX, Fukushima, and Challenger) to demonstrate how society successfully investigates failures through independent searchers and root-cause analysis—and contrasts this with the systemic failure to uncover the origins of COVID-19.
briefings.summary_markdown:
## TL;DR
Bill Gurley examines historical catastrophes (like the 737 MAX, Fukushima, and Challenger) to demonstrate how society successfully investigates failures through independent searchers and root-cause analysis—and contrasts this with the systemic failure to uncover the origins of COVID-19.

## Catastrophic Investigations & The CAPA Framework
- **The Corrective and Preventive Action (CAPA) Framework:** A five-step scientific process used in pharmaceuticals, medical devices, and aerospace (Detect, Investigate, Confirm root cause, Correct, Prevent) where skipping root-cause analysis makes prevention impossible.
- **Surfside, Florida Condo Collapse (June 2021):** 
  - **Casualties & Cost:** 98 deaths.
  - **Investigation:** Four parallel investigations, including NIST, Alan Kilsheimer, a Florida grand jury, 17 consolidated victim lawsuits, and the *Miami Herald* (staffing 37 people, winning a Pulitzer Prize).
  - **Outcome:** Led to major rule changes in Florida and coastal states to prevent future collapses.
- **Boeing 737 MAX Crashes (Oct 2018 / Mar 2019):**
  - **Root Cause:** A fuel-efficient engine was attached forward on an older airframe, causing an imbalance; secret software called MCAS pushed the plane down during sensor malfunctions.
  - **Investigation:** Six search groups included US Senate/House commissions, the DOJ, Indonesia's KNKT, *Seattle Times* reporter Dominic Gates (Pulitzer winner), 57 whistleblowers, and the pilots' union (who recorded meetings and filed FOIA requests).
  - **Blockers:** Boeing and the FAA acted as blockers, initially blaming pilots and refusing document requests; 45 days after the first crash, the plane was still not grounded, leading to a preventable second crash.
- **Hurricane Katrina (2005):**
  - **Casualties & Cost:** 1,800 deaths, 400,000 displaced, $125 billion in damage.
  - **Root Cause:** Levees washed out from underneath during a Category 3 hurricane due to man-made engineering errors by the US Army Corps of Engineers.
  - **Investigation:** House/Senate commissions, Pulitzer-winning journalists (Mark Schleifstein and John McQuaid), NSF-backed UC professors, and an LSU team.
  - **Blockers:** The Army Corps of Engineers attempted to block investigations and encapsulated the American Society of Civil Engineers (ASCE) after paying them $1 million.
  - **Outcome:** Led to 90 recommendations and $15 billion in sea walls that have held for 20 years.
- **Fukushima Nuclear Disaster (2011):**
  - **Casualties & Cost:** 2,200 deaths, 154,000 displaced, $200 billion in cleanup.
  - **Root Cause:** A seawall of 5.7 meters was overtopped by tsunamis (internal reports showed expected tsunamis of 10-15 meters were buried).
  - **Investigation:** Led by Dr. Kyoshi Kurokawa heading Japan's first-ever private parliamentary commission with zero institutional ties to regulators or the power company.
- **Space Shuttle Challenger Disaster (January 1986):**
  - **Root Cause:** O-rings on solid rocket boosters failed in cold weather.
  - **Searcher:** Caltech physicist Richard Feynman served on the Rogers Commission, cleared his schedule for six months, conducted independent investigations, and famously demonstrated the O-ring failure with ice water on live television.

## COVID-19 Origins & The Absence of Investigation
- **Scale of Impact:** 15 million deaths, $45 trillion in global cost, and severe learning loss for children—making COVID-19 3,000 times larger in cost and death toll than the combined five historical catastrophes ($349B, 5,000 deaths).
- **The Missing Search Infrastructure:** Unlike smaller historical disasters, COVID-19 lacked committed newsrooms with 30+ investigators, bipartisan congressional committees, NIH/NSF-funded third-party scientific investigations, or massive victim lawsuits.
- **The "Blocker" Insiders:** Francis Collins, Anthony Fauci, Peter Daszak (EcoHealth Alliance), Jeremy Farrar (Wellcome Trust/WHO), and Ralph Baric (UNC) acted as blockers due to:
  - Being virology insiders protecting their institution.
  - Leading a misinformation campaign to discourage searching.
  - Being outspoken prior advocates of **Gain-of-Function** research (intentionally making viruses more dangerous).
  - Failing to ever launch a search.
- **The Heroes and Searchers:**
  - **Alina Chan:** Molecular biologist who co-authored a book; wrote two op-eds published by *The New York Times*.
  - **Katherine Eban:** Wrote a foundational *Vanity Fair* article ("The Fight to Discover COVID Origins") detailing the discovery blockade.
  - **Emily Kopp:** Uncovered the majority of FOIA documents working for U.S. Right to Know.
  - **Zeynep Tufekci:** Princeton professor and writer who exposed the coordinated cover-up.
  - **Alison Young:** Author of *Pandora's Gamble*, examining prior lab leak failures.
  - **Drastic:** A loosely affiliated group of independent scientist-researchers.
  - **U.S. Right to Know:** A nonprofit filing FOIA requests to uncover key documents.

## The Misinformation Campaign & The Defuse Proposal
- **Manufactured Consensus:** Insiders leveraged scientific journals to quickly publish papers (such as the *Proximal Origins* paper and *The Lancet* statement) to steer public narrative toward natural spillover and label lab-leak inquiries as conspiracy theories.
- **The Defuse Proposal:** Uncovered by Drastic three years post-outbreak, this proposal by Peter Daszak’s EcoHealth Alliance detailed plans to insert a furin cleavage site at the S1/S2 junction of a bat coronavirus to increase viral infectivity. Major scientific journals and 78% of surveyed scientists were unaware of it.
- **Current Institutional Obstructions:** University of North Carolina (UNC) and the State of North Carolina have refused to deliver documents requested by searchers regarding gain-of-function research.

## Notable Quotes
> *"The accident at the power plant cannot be regarded as a natural disaster, it was profoundly man-made disaster and it could and should have been foreseen and prevented."*
> — **Dr. Kyoshi Kurokawa**

> *"We can easily forgive a child who is afraid of the dark; the real tragedy of life is when men are afraid of the light."*
> — **Plato (Cited by Bill Gurley)**

> *"Indisputable proof of a conspiracy to cover up and deny the possibility it well may be a lab mishap, orchestrated from the highest levels of the scientific establishment and a self-serving group of scientists who deliberately misled the public."*
> — **Zeynep Tufekci**

briefings.title: The Evolving AI Landscape: A Conversation between SpaceX CFO Bret Johnsen and BlackRock's Tony Kim
briefings.tldr: SpaceX Chief Financial Officer Bret Johnsen and BlackRock Global Technology Team Head Tony Kim discussed SpaceX's rapid scaling into AI infrastructure, projecting over $100 billion in annualized run rate (ARR) by the end of 2026, driven by a 1-year terrestrial compute payback and upcoming orbital compute deployments starting next year.
briefings.summary_markdown:
### TL;DR
SpaceX Chief Financial Officer Bret Johnsen and BlackRock Global Technology Team Head Tony Kim discussed SpaceX's rapid scaling into AI infrastructure, projecting over $100 billion in annualized run rate (ARR) by the end of 2026, driven by a 1-year terrestrial compute payback and upcoming orbital compute deployments starting next year.

## SpaceX's AI Infrastructure & Financial Scale
* **Rapid Revenue Growth:** 
  * SpaceX went from **$0** in AI revenue a year ago to an annualized run rate (ARR) projection of over **$100 billion** by the end of December 2026 (inclusive of total company revenue, with AI comprising the majority).
* **Terrestrial Compute Expansion:** 
  * SpaceX is on track to exit 2026 with **a little over 2 gigawatts** of terrestrial compute capacity.
  * Guidance targets scaling to **5 to 10 gigawatts** by the end of next year.
* **Vertical Integration Advantage:** 
  * Leveraging in-house engineering for data centers, power systems, cooling, and networking allows SpaceX to avoid margin stacking and move rapidly.
  * Former aerospace talent (accustomed to pressurized fuels and gases) is directly applying engineering discipline to data center design and high-power systems.
* **Hosting and Monetization Strategy:** 
  * Operates a flexible hosting model for tier-one customers like Anthropic and Google, using short-term commitments (3-month contracts with 3-month options, effectively 6-month terms).
  * Achieves a **dramatically less than 1-year payback** on cutting-edge terrestrial compute.

## Software, Frontier Models, & Products
* **Catching the Frontier:** 
  * While OpenAI and Anthropic currently sit at the bleeding edge of Artificial General Intelligence (AGI), SpaceX (via xAI) is closing the gap rapidly.
  * Five major players currently form the front tier of the industry, with weekly releases of new model functionality.
* **Ecosystem and Content Integration:** 
  * Integrating **X** provides a massive content advantage with **500M to nearly 600M monthly active users**.
  * **Grokbot** is experiencing viral growth faster than any product the company has previously seen.
  * **Cursor** integration is driving internal design efficiencies and external developer tooling improvements.

## Starship and Orbital Compute
* **Starship 14 and V3 Satellites:** 
  * The upcoming Starship 14 launch (later this month) marks the deployment of commercial **Version 3 broadband satellites** into orbit.
  * A single Starship launch with V3 satellites delivers **20 times the capacity** of previous Falcon 9 flights, yielding **50 terabits** of downlink bandwidth per launch.
* **Reusability Timeline:** 
  * Flight 15 (the flight following Starship 14) will target full first- and second-stage reusability, aiming for meaningful re-flights next year.
* **Orbital Compute Economics:** 
  * Starship drives a **10x improvement in cost per kilogram to orbit**.
  * By the end of the decade, SpaceX aims to deploy **100 gigawatts per year** in space-based compute.
  * Orbital compute benefits from falling chip costs (Moore's Law) and **free, clean energy** from solar/space fusion, avoiding terrestrial power grid, cooling, and regulatory bottlenecks.

## Manufacturing & Supply Chain Constraints
* **Power and Turbine Bottlenecks:** 
  * Gas turbine supply chains are heavily constrained (18 to 24-month lead times for blades and vanes) due to sudden multi-fold demand from the AI industry.
  * SpaceX is standing up an in-house investment casting facility to pour metal and build necessary turbine components itself.
* **Terafab Concept:** 
  * To bypass long-term semiconductor and memory fab capacity constraints (where memory is projected to grow ~30% annually against triple-digit AI demand), SpaceX is pursuing the "Terafab" concept.
  * The goal is to see real volume benefits from development versions (partnering with Tesla next year, moving to 2028/2029 production) to support the orbital AI hockey-stick ramp.

---

## Predictions & Forward Calls
* **Bret Johnsen:** SpaceX will exit 2026 with an annualized run rate (ARR) of over **$100 billion**.
* **Bret Johnsen:** Terrestrial compute capacity will reach a little over **2 gigawatts** by the end of 2026.
* **Bret Johnsen:** Terrestrial compute capacity will scale to **5 to 10 gigawatts** by the end of next year (2027).
* **Bret Johnsen:** SpaceX will fly its first space-based data center equivalent satellites (orbital compute racks) at the end of next year.
* **Bret Johnsen:** SpaceX is on track to put up **100 gigawatts per year** of orbital compute by the end of the decade.
* **Bret Johnsen:** Tesla will develop a development version of the Terafab next year, with real volume benefits expected by 2028 and meaningful contribution by 2029 and beyond.

---

## Notable Quotes
> *"If you look at I think the core one of the core differentiations of SpaceX as a whole and then certainly our AI approach, it's the vertical integration. Right? It's the fact that we do almost everything in-house."* — **Bret Johnsen**

> *"Right now what that's translating into is dramatically less than one year payback on cutting edge compute in the terrestrial [market]. And so we can continue to invest in a meaningful way."* — **Bret Johnsen**

> *"Everyone else thinks this is like a decade away. We're going to start flying our first ones next year. Right? So, I think that's going to be... That'll be the shock."* — **Bret Johnsen**

> *"You're putting up 20% of the United States improvement of the entire US grid every year. And we're just going to keep going, right? Elon's talking about a terawatt in space... when you get into the 2030s."* — **Bret Johnsen**
